name: Packaging & Distribution

objectives.text: Identify common materials used to package food such as glass, metal, paper, cardboard, and plastic
Classify foods by whether they must be kept refrigerated, frozen, or shelf stable while they are stored and shipped
Describe how packaging protects food from crushing, moisture, light, air, and pests during shipping and storage
Identify the information printed on a food package such as ingredients, net weight, date codes, and handling instructions
Explain how temperature, humidity, and rough handling during transport affect the quality of perishable foods such as milk, meat, and fresh produce
Explain how packaging design features such as seals, barriers, and tamper evident closures affect a food product's shelf life and safety
Package and label a farm product for direct sale at a farmers market or FFA fruit sale using safe handling practices
Summarize food packaging methods including canning, retort pouches, vacuum packaging, aseptic packaging, and modified atmosphere packaging
Explain how the cold chain uses temperature control during storage and transport to maintain food safety and quality
Select appropriate packaging materials for fresh, frozen, and ready to eat food products based on each product's storage needs
Analyze changes in color, texture, flavor, and moisture of a food stored in different packaging through a shelf life test
Apply safe food handling procedures for receiving, storing, and loading food products such as first in first out rotation and temperature logging
Interpret federal labeling requirements on food packages including the nutrition facts panel, allergen declarations, and date labeling
Analyze packaging options for a food product based on cost, protection, and sustainability
Evaluate the environmental impact of different food packaging materials across their life cycle from production to disposal or recycling
Assess how market demand influences the distribution channels and packaging formats used for a food product
Recommend improvements to safety procedures in a food distribution scenario to ensure a safe product reaches consumers
Create a distribution plan for a food product that ensures safe delivery through temperature control, transport selection, and product traceability
Design a packaging solution for a food product that balances protection, cost, and sustainability
Create a plan to educate consumers or the community about sustainable food packaging and reducing food waste

changes: Kept all six original objectives, rewording grades 5, 7, 11, and 12 for precision. Added early objectives on storage classification, package labels, and transport conditions. Added a grade 8 SAE and FFA packaging objective. Added grades 9 to 12 objectives on packaging methods, the cold chain, material selection, shelf life testing, safe handling during distribution, labeling regulations, market demand, safety recommendations, distribution planning, and sustainability education. These are aligned to AFNR FPP standards. Broader supply chain and product formulation content was left to the sibling sub-topics.
